title: Piano Trio in C major, Hob. XV:C1

title: Piano Trio in G major, Hob. XIV:6

(2) That print is titled 'pour le clavecin', so the pre-1770 keyboard rule would give a harpsichord trio. Left unchanged.

title: Triptych for High Voice and String Quartet

title: Opusculum Neuwer Paduanen, Gaillarden, Couranten und Volten
note: IMSLP lists 30 pieces incl. pavans by Dowland (3), Tomkins and Farmer (2): a mixed-authorship anthology, not wholly Simpson's own; scoring is '5 instruments' (violin alternative unsourced); only selections recorded (Galliard no. 18; CPO has 3 pairs). Owner to rule whether it passes the floor/own-work rule

title: String Quartet No. 4 ("My Mother's Songs")
note: Numbering unsafe: 'Pjesme moje majke' (1940) is a cycle for alto and string quartet (or string orchestra) (sr.wikipedia); Slavenski's String Quartet No. 4 is listed as 1938 and CPO (Sebastian Qt, 15:08) records it as his own transcription of the Balkan Dances. Zagreb Qt tracks 12:58 label the songs 'No. 4'. Title/aka need the owner's decision

title: Quartet in E-flat major, Op. 8 No. 2
note: Title, key, 1773 and scoring (IMSLP lists horn/bassoon substitutes) hold, but the only recording found, Claves 'Blaesermusik der Klassik' (10:28), is a wind version for oboe, clarinet, horn and bassoon (the disc text, seen in a search; IMSLP's Weigelt arrangement has the same forces), not the scoring described; no recording with strings found, while Op. 8 Nos. 1, 3, 4 have them

title: Trio in G major for Two Flutes and Cello, Op. 14 No. 1
note: Piece exists and is recorded (Nimbus NI 5967, 2017, 13:13), but 'Op. 14 No. 1' is only the recording's label: Bärenreiter Hortus Musicus 106 (per IMSLP) shows no opus, IMSLP says it is not the Welcker Op. 14, and the Welcker No. 1 in G (Moderato, Andante moderato, Rondo) is the separate trio 102056. An opus number that cannot be confirmed should leave the title

title: Trio in G major for Two Flutes and Cello, Op. 14 No. 2
note: Recorded (Nimbus 16:06; Berlin Classics lists the same movements as 'Trio in G major', 13:52), but 'Op. 14 No. 2' is only Nimbus's label: the Welcker Op. 14 No. 2 is in C major (movements in Multisonic listing), so this is another G-major trio and the opus number is unconfirmed

title: Sinfonia a tre
note: Title has no key and Stradella left several sinfonie a tre: Giardino di Delizie records No. 1 in D minor (8:08) and No. 2 in B-flat (7:10), L'Accademico Formato one in D major (6:43), CPO a 5:40 single. IMSLP's page (Antiqua 4657, Kolneder 1956) gives no key, so the recording cannot be tied to this edition. A 'Sinfonia a tre' recording does exist; add a key if one can be established.

title: Quemadmodum
note: Recorded on viols (Savall, Alia Vox, 5:00), and IMSLP says '6 instruments, most likely viol consort', but Wikipedia/CPDL (via search) say it is now thought to be a six-part motet on Psalm 42 (Vulgate 41) found untexted in the Baldwin partbooks: possibly a vocal work played on viols, not an original consort piece. Owner's call on scope

title: Trio Sonata in C minor, TWV 42:c8
note: Exists (TWV catalogue, IMSLP: 2 violins, 4 mvts) but no complete recording found: the only one (Kooij/L'Armonia Sonora, Passacaille 2018) has just 'I. Affetuoso' (1:31) as an interlude; MusicBrainz recording search shows nothing else; IMSLP has MS parts only

title: Trio Sonata in D major, TWV 42:D10
note: Exists (RISM Darmstadt Mus.ms 1042/62; TWV catalogue: 'Intrada' for flute, violin, bc, 6 mvts incl. Tournee, Aria, Menuet alternativo, Trio, Balletto, so suite-like, no Presto). The cited Zefirelli track 'IV. Presto' (1:54) and the Biondi and Extempore tracks labelled 'D10' are TWV 42:d10 in D minor (Allegro-Adagio-Allegro-Presto, same as Chandos Baroque Players and Il Rossignolo). No recording of the D major Intrada found

title: Trio Sonata in E minor, TWV 42:e9
note: Exists and is recorded (Epoca Barocca, CPO 2011, 6:51; mvts Largo-Allegro-Affettuoso-Vivace) but the scoring may be wrong: TWV catalogue says 'flute, oboe, bc' and the Darmstadt MS (RISM 450002853, Mus.ms 1042/61) is 'Flute-Traversiere, Hautbois, Basse', no strings; only IMSLP (Dresden parts, Garty edition) gives 2 violins. If violins are not original the work is out of scope (no string part)

title: Quartet in D major, TWV 43:D5
note: Exists (TWV catalogue: 2 violins, viola, bc; Allemande-Ballo-Giga). The only recording found is on a 111-track budget compilation by 'The Telemann Society Orchestra' (Menuetto Classics), an orchestra, so not shown to be one to a part; no published edition (IMSLP: MS and a private typeset); no MusicBrainz entry

title: Petit quatuor à cordes
note: IMSLP (Hamelle, c. 1909) shows a five-movement quartet in G major/minor (Maestoso-Allegro moderato, Lento, Menuetto, Allegro energico, Arabeske), not a three-minute miniature. The Nota Bene album has only 'Petit Quatuor a Cordes in G Minor: V. Arabesce' (3:05); no recording of the whole work found. If kept: minutes unknown (about 12-15?), notes wrong.

title: Flute Quartet in B-flat major, Op. 2 No. 4
note: Recording exists (Hoffmusic Mannheim, RBM, 'Flute Quartet in B-flat major, Op. 2 No. 4', 3:31+3:58; Apple Classical credits C. Toeschi). But IMSLP lists Toeschi's flute-quartet sets as Op. 1, Op. 3, Op. 5 and unnumbered manuscripts (a B-flat quartet is No. 4 of '5 Quartets'); no source for an 'Op. 2' besides the disc's labelling. Opus unconfirmed; if the owner will not keep an unconfirmed number, drop 'Op. 2 No. 4' from title and set.

title: String Quartet in B-flat major, Op. 8
note: Recorded (Hungaroton, 31:00, four movements, which fits Op. 8) and Deezer tags it 'Op. 8', but no source gives the keys of Op. 8, so the opus rests on that tag. Year 'c. 1780' is IMSLP's guess for a Vienna print with Steiner/Haslinger imprint (plate 579); a review calls this piece a 1790s work. Year doubtful.

title: String Quartet in D minor, Op. 8
note: Recorded (Hungaroton, 24:44, four movements, which fits Op. 8) and Deezer tags it 'Op. 8', but no source gives the keys of Op. 8, so the opus rests on that tag. Year 'c. 1780' doubtful as for the B-flat quartet.

title: Balla d'amore
note: Only recording found (Parley of Instruments, Hyperion CDA66240) is credited 'Arr. Philips for String Ensemble' and played by a consort of renaissance violins and violas, not viols; Hyperion's notes say Tregian's score-book section holds Philips's arrangements and original pieces, and that Tregian was mainly the copyist. Unclear whether Tregian composed the piece and whether the 5-viol IMSLP edition is Philips's own arrangement; leans to arrangement / not recorded on viols

title: Eight Miniatures on Georgian Folk Tunes
note: Wikipedia lists 'Eight Miniatures on Georgian Folk Tunes' (1988), but the only 8-track recording (St Petersburg Classics 1994) is titled just 'Miniatures ... Based on Georgian Folksongs' and mixes pieces from earlier sets (Indi Mindi and Sachidao are in the 1945 Three Miniatures; Firefly is in the Twelve). The Georgian catalogue has sets of 21, 5, 6 and 8 Miniatures. Not shown that the disc is the 1988 set. The Caprice album (2004) holds other numbered sets, not these eight

title: Aria seconda sopra E' tanto tempo hormai, Op. 3
note: Only recording found is sixty1strings (mandolin/harp/guitar group), Genuin 2022, track 'Op. 3: No. 2, Aria' 4:28; not shown to be this aria or played on violins. Other Uccellini discs lack it

title: Sinfonia a tre, Op. 1 No. 12 ("per il Santissimo Natale")
note: Work exists (Op. 1, Rome 1701). Floor: every recording found is by a directed band (Northwest CO, NZ CO) or Cappella Gabetta (Sony, strings and continuo, personnel unknown); none shown one to a part. Roger part-books give violins I/II, cello, continuo. Out as string-orchestra question unless a one-to-a-part recording turns up

title: Trio Sonata in G major, Op. 3
note: Recorded (Musica da camera Praga, Supraphon 1979; 3 movements, 10:38) under the title 'Sonata for Flute, Violin and Continuo in G Major, Op. 3', but 'Op. 3' is not in IMSLP, Wikipedia's list or klassika; no Weinmann number found. If still unconfirmed, drop 'Op. 3' from the title (keep as aka)

title: Alpha, O. 58
note: Facts hold (IMSLP: 7 min, 2015, clarinet version; NACUSA SF concert 7 Nov 2015). But the only evidence is one concert of a composers' society ensemble, no recording, self-published CC0 scores: professional track record not shown.

title: Despite It, O. 104
note: Facts hold (IMSLP: 9.5 min, 2022, flute version; our 10 min is right, IMSLP mismatch is not real). Same doubt as Alpha: one NACUSA SF composers' ensemble concert, no recording, self-published; professional track record not shown.

title: Artificii musicali, Op. 13
note: IMSLP gives 60 pieces for 2-12 instruments (a contrapuntal textbook, Grove); recordings are single pieces (Violin Sonatas Nos 1-2 for violin and bass, No. 53 Balletto), not the set. Scoring '2 violins + continuo' does not hold for the whole opus; owner to decide whether it belongs as one entry

title: Trio No. 9 in G major
note: Key conflict: Deezer/Apple track titles say 'Trio No. 9 in G major', retailer pages of the same CPO release (Europadisc, Radio Times) say 'no.9 in A major'. Work exists and is recorded; key unresolved. The note 'recording of 17 trios' should read 7 of 17 (as fixed for the sister entries)

title: String Quartet No. 2 in E major
note: Urania and Wikipedia title it 'String Quartet No. 2 in E major with Viola d'amore (1906)'; IMSLP lists 2 vn, va, vc. The viola part may be for viola d'amore (Urania violist plays both). 25:50, 1906 hold.

title: String Quartet No. 5 in E-flat major, Op. 81
note: Existence, key (E-flat), Op. 81, scoring, 4 movements, cpo recording (24:32) confirmed; the year 1931 found in no source (not on IMSLP, no work list gives a date)

title: Gantz Neue Cantzon, Intraden, Balletten und Courranten
note: Print (1618, 4 and 5 parts, 'sonderlich auff Violen') confirmed; floor weak: only Canzona, Gaillard, Intrada (about 6 min) on a 1975 Cantilena/Grange 'Christmas Concerto' disc (not a viol consort); no other recording found on Deezer or MusicBrainz

title: Sonata for Piano Four Hands and Violin in G minor, Op. 42
note: Title page of the Breitkopf print reads 'avec Flute ou Violon', flute first, and the only recording found (Euridice, 25.4 min) uses flute. Entry makes violin the main part and flute the alternative, which is the reverse; with flute first the work would have no string part. No recording with violin found. Owner to decide scope and order

title: Big Beautiful Dark and Scary
note: Duration conflict: the composer's list and Corelia give 15 min (2002, six players, one movement); the only recording (Bang on a Can All-Stars, Cantaloupe) runs 8:44 on Deezer and 8.7 on Apple. Entry has 9. If 15 is right the form becomes 'work'. The notes' 'also an orchestral version' is not on the composer's list; worth a second look

title: String Quartet No. 1, Op. 1
note: Facts hold (IMSLP: 4 movements, 10 min, 2023) and the own-label Apple Music album 'Agape' (P 2025 Mike Zak, performers not credited) names the work, so the floor is met under the owner's own-label rule. But no professional track record found: only self-published IMSLP scores (CC licence) and his own album; a web search found no performance, commission, publisher or established-label release. Owner to rule on the track-record condition.

title: String Trio in D major, Op. 2 No. 3
note: Recorded (Vivaldi Project, MSR MS 1623, 2021, 'Trio in D Major, Op. 2, No. 3', 8:53) so the floor is met, but scoring and opus cannot be pinned: IMSLP's Op. 2 is 6 quintets, de/it Wikipedia list several 'op. 2' sets incl. 6 trios for violin, viola and cello (Perugia, 1781) and 6 trio sonatas for 2 violins; the players switch violin/viola. 2 violins + cello is unconfirmed (could be violin, viola, cello). Keep the recording's Op. number or drop it once a source is found

title: Piano Quartet
note: Work holds (IMSLP: 2005, violin/viola/cello/piano, 3 mvts; album 25:24) and the album names professional players, but the only recording is the composer's own release (P Wim Zwaag, 2006) and I found no independent performance, publisher or commission, so the composer track record is not established.

title: Piano Trio
note: Work holds (IMSLP: 'Requiem', 2005, 4 mvts; album 26:38, a track mislabelled 'V.'); same caveat: only the composer's own release is found, so his professional track record is not established.
